title: Protocol for quantifying the adhesive strength of single fluorescent cells adhering to a non-fluorescent cell monolayer by fluidic force microscopy
author: Gunaratnam, Oh, et al.

steps.title: Thaw and seed fibroblasts
steps.instruction: Thaw one vial of cryopreserved fibroblasts (500 000 cells) and seed into a T75 culture flask containing DMEM supplemented with 15 % fetal calf serum (FCS).

steps.title: Cultivate fibroblasts to sub‑confluence
steps.instruction: Incubate the flask at 37 °C, 95 % humidity, 5 % CO₂ and change the medium three times per week until the cells reach sub‑confluence.

steps.title: Create confluent monolayer in fluorodish
steps.instruction: Two days before the experiment (day −2), seed fibroblasts at 110 cells mm⁻² in 2.5 mL DMEM + 15 % FCS inside a fluorodish to obtain a confluent monolayer.

steps.title: Seed fluorescent cells for overlay
steps.instruction: Also on day −2, seed the same‑passage fibroblasts at 50 cells mm⁻² in 3 mL into a cavity of a 6‑well plate; the next day (day −1) stain these cells with a fluorophore.

steps.title: Stain cells with CMFDA
steps.instruction: On day 0, remove medium from the 6‑well plate, wash the cells with sterile PBS, add pre‑warmed staining solution (20 µM CMFDA in serum‑free DMEM) and incubate 1 h; then discard the stain, rinse twice with PBS, add DMEM + 15 % FCS and incubate another 1 h.

steps.title: Seed labeled cells on monolayer
steps.instruction: Trypsinize the CMFDA‑labeled cells and seed them onto the confluent monolayer in the fluorodish at 4 cells mm⁻²; allow adhesion for 3 h in DMEM + 15 % FCS before FluidFM experiments.

steps.title: Calibrate FluidFM system
steps.instruction: Power on the AFM controller, microfluidic system, computer and optical microscope; start AFM and microscope software; wait up to 1 h for laser stabilization; mount the micropipette on the cantilever holder, fill its back‑reservoir with 10 µL 50 % glycerol, connect the pneumatic line and mount the pipette on the AFM scan head; bring the pipette into view with a 10× objective, align the laser on the tip, tilt the photodiode to centre the reflection; calibrate the spring constant in air using the thermal‑tune function; press glycerol through the channel at 1 bar (glycerol should exit the tip after 1.5–2 min); place a fresh fluorodish on the stage, add 50 µL FluidFM medium, re‑mount the scan head so the pipette is fully immersed (add a small drop of medium if needed); let the pipette equilibrate, then re‑align the laser and photodiode; approach the dish surface automatically, calibrate crosstalk and deflection sensitivity; the pipette is now ready for experiments (do not move the laser afterwards).

steps.title: Prepare dish for FluidFM SCFS
steps.instruction: Replace the supernatant in the fluorodish with 1 mL FluidFM medium, minimize ambient light to reduce bleaching, fix the dish on the AFM stage and verify that the micropipette tip is fully immersed by visual inspection and by confirming laser signal intensity in the AFM software.

steps.title: Position micropipette and locate fluorescent cell
steps.instruction: Switch to camera mode, focus with the 10× objective, manually advance the pipette until it is just out of focus (blurred view); set a force setpoint of 20–50 nN and click “Approach” for a force‑controlled approach to the cell layer; switch to eyepieces, select 50× magnification, set stage height to −20 µm; align the pipette opening with the eyepiece cross‑line using the X/Y manual adjustments; briefly press “Retract” (1–2 s) to lift the pipette slightly without leaving the liquid; switch to fluorescence mode (e.g., Zeiss 38 HE filter) and search for a fluorescent cell with the joystick; approach the pipette next to the cell with a 20 nN setpoint, then lower stage height to −100 µm and centre the pipette opening over the cell; click “Approach” again to make contact and verify centring in bright‑field mode.

steps.title: Perform force‑distance measurement
steps.instruction: Start a force‑distance sweep with the following parameters: ramp height 100 µm, approach/retract speed 2 µm s⁻¹ (range 1–10 µm s⁻¹), ramp time 50 s, 50 000 data points, target force 20 nN (adjustable 10–70 nN), contact time 5 s, apply −700 mbar negative pressure for 55 s beginning at contact; observe cell detachment live via the camera.

steps.title: Detach cell and verify fluorescence
steps.instruction: After detachment, move the stage laterally with the joystick to look for any remaining anchoring points; if none are seen, the cell is fully detached; switch to eyepieces, fluorescence mode and slowly move the pipette laterally—if the cell fluoresces, the detached cell is immobilised on the pipette and the experiment succeeded.

steps.title: Save force curve data
steps.instruction: Save the force‑distance curve file for later post‑processing.

steps.title: Clean and store FluidFM probe
steps.instruction: Prepare ~50 µL of filtered 5 % sodium hypochlorite cleaning solution in a fluorodish; also prepare a second dish with three 50 µL drops of salt‑free water spaced apart and a third dish with a single 50 µL drop of FluidFM medium; immerse the mounted micropipette in the cleaning solution, apply −50 mbar for 10 s then +100 mbar for 10 s, expel the solution; remove excess liquid with a Kimtech wipe (avoid touching the tip); sequentially transfer the pipette into the water drops to rinse, wipe dry again, equilibrate in FluidFM medium before reuse; for long‑term storage (up to 4 weeks) keep the dried pipette in its original cantilever package, seal with film and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Process force‑distance data
steps.instruction: Open the raw curve as a force‑distance (height) trace in analysis software (e.g., SPIP); perform baseline correction on the approach curve to define the 0 nN level (baseline may be verified on a glass control curve); save the corrected curve as an ASCII file; import the ASCII file into Excel and transfer height (X) and force (Y) values to the chosen analysis program (e.g., OriginPro); integrate the area under the retract curve down to the baseline to obtain adhesion energy and read the most negative force value as the adhesion force; if the full detachment is recorded, the final negative force corresponds to the cell detachment length on the x‑axis.
